passages.text: Soon the people began to complain about their hardship in the hearing of the LORD, and when He heard them, His anger was kindled, and fire from the LORD blazed among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel began to complain about their hardship.
The LORD heard their complaints.
The LORD became angry.
Fire from the LORD burned among the people.
The fire consumed the outskirts of the camp.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י הָעָם֙ כְּמִתְאֹ֣נְנִ֔ים רַ֖ע בְּאָזְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יְהוָה֙ וַיִּ֣חַר אַפּ֔וֹ וַתִּבְעַר־ בָּם֙ אֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה וַתֹּ֖אכַל בִּקְצֵ֥ה הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: And the people cried out to Moses, and he prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
passages.sermon: The people cried out to Moses.\r\nMoses prayed to the LORD.\r\nThe fire died down.
passages.original: וַיִּצְעַ֥ק הָעָ֖ם אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֤ל מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה וַתִּשְׁקַ֖ע הָאֵֽשׁ׃

passages.text: So that place was called Taberah, because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel traveled in the wilderness.
They complained against the LORD.
The LORD became angry.
He sent fire among them.
The fire burned at the edge of their camp.
Moses prayed to the LORD.
The fire stopped.
They named that place Taberah.
They called it Taberah because the fire of the LORD had burned among them.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֛א שֵֽׁם־ הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא תַּבְעֵרָ֑ה כִּֽי־ בָעֲרָ֥ה בָ֖ם אֵ֥שׁ יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, the rabble among them had a strong craving for other food, and again the Israelites wept and said, “Who will feed us meat?
passages.sermon:
A group of people called the rabble lived among the Israelites.
The rabble wanted other food very much.
They felt a strong craving.
The Israelites also began to cry again.
The Israelites said, “Who will give us meat to eat?”
passages.original: וְהָֽאסַפְסֻף֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ הִתְאַוּ֖וּ תַּאֲוָ֑ה וַיָּשֻׁ֣בוּ וַיִּבְכּ֗וּ גַּ֚ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ מִ֥י יַאֲכִלֵ֖נוּ בָּשָֽׂר׃

passages.text: We remember the fish we ate freely in Egypt, along with the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites spoke.
They remembered their time in Egypt.
They said, “We remember the fish we ate in Egypt.
We ate the fish without cost.
We also remember the cucumbers.
We remember the melons.
We remember the leeks.
We remember the onions.
We remember the garlic.”
passages.original: זָכַ֙רְנוּ֙ אֶת־ הַדָּגָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־ נֹאכַ֥ל בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם חִנָּ֑ם אֵ֣ת הַקִּשֻּׁאִ֗ים וְאֵת֙ הָֽאֲבַטִּחִ֔ים וְאֶת־ הֶחָצִ֥יר וְאֶת־ הַבְּצָלִ֖ים וְאֶת־ הַשּׁוּמִֽים׃

passages.text: But now our appetite is gone; there is nothing to see but this manna!”
passages.sermon:
The Israelites traveled in the wilderness.
They received manna from God as their food.
Now the Israelites felt tired and discouraged.
They lost their appetite.
They saw nothing except manna.
They had no other food to eat.
Their eyes looked only at the manna.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֛ה נַפְשֵׁ֥נוּ יְבֵשָׁ֖ה אֵ֣ין כֹּ֑ל בִּלְתִּ֖י אֶל־ הַמָּ֥ן עֵינֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: Now the manna resembled coriander seed, and its appearance was like that of gum resin.
passages.sermon: The manna was a special food from God.\r\nThe manna looked like coriander seed.\r\nThe manna’s appearance was like gum resin.
passages.original: וְהַמָּ֕ן כִּזְרַע־ גַּ֖ד ה֑וּא וְעֵינ֖וֹ כְּעֵ֥ין הַבְּדֹֽלַח׃

passages.text: The people walked around and gathered it, ground it on a handmill or crushed it in a mortar, then boiled it in a cooking pot or shaped it into cakes. It tasted like pastry baked with fine oil.
passages.sermon:
The people are the Israelites.
The Israelites walked around.
They gathered the manna.
They ground the manna in a handmill.
Or they crushed the manna in a mortar.
They boiled the manna in a cooking pot.
Or they shaped the manna into cakes.
The manna tasted like pastry baked with fine oil.
passages.original: שָׁטוּ֩ הָעָ֨ם וְלָֽקְט֜וּ וְטָחֲנ֣וּ בָרֵחַ֗יִם א֤וֹ דָכוּ֙ בַּמְּדֹכָ֔ה וּבִשְּׁלוּ֙ בַּפָּר֔וּר וְעָשׂ֥וּ אֹת֖וֹ עֻג֑וֹת וְהָיָ֣ה טַעְמ֔וֹ כְּטַ֖עַם לְשַׁ֥ד הַשָּֽׁמֶן׃

passages.text: When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna would fall with it.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites camped in the wilderness.
At night, dew fell on their camp.
When the dew fell, manna also fell on the camp.
Manna came down together with the dew.
passages.original: וּבְרֶ֧דֶת הַטַּ֛ל עַל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה לָ֑יְלָה יֵרֵ֥ד הַמָּ֖ן עָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Moses heard the people of family after family weeping at the entrances to their tents, and the anger of the LORD was kindled greatly, and Moses was also displeased.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
The Israelites were living in tents in the wilderness.
Moses heard the people crying.
Each family was weeping.
Each person sat at the entrance of his tent and cried.
The LORD became very angry.
Moses also became displeased.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֨ע מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת־ הָעָ֗ם בֹּכֶה֙ לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָ֔יו אִ֖ישׁ לְפֶ֣תַח אָהֳל֑וֹ וַיִּֽחַר־ אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ מְאֹ֔ד וּבְעֵינֵ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה רָֽע׃

passages.text: So Moses asked the LORD, “Why have You brought this trouble on Your servant? Why have I not found favor in Your sight, that You have laid upon me the burden of all these people?
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses said, “Why have You brought trouble on me, Your servant?”
Moses asked, “Why have I not found favor in Your eyes?”
Moses said, “You have put the burden of all these people on me.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־ יְהוָ֗ה לָמָ֤ה הֲרֵעֹ֙תָ֙ לְעַבְדֶּ֔ךָ וְלָ֛מָּה לֹא־ מָצָ֥תִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ לָשׂ֗וּם אֶת־ מַשָּׂ֛א כָּל־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה עָלָֽי׃

passages.text: Did I conceive all these people? Did I give them birth, so that You should tell me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries an infant,’ to the land that You swore to give their fathers?
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Moses said, "Did I conceive all these people?"
Moses said, "Did I give birth to them?"
Moses said, "You tell me to carry them in my arms."
Moses said, "You want me to carry them as a nurse carries an infant."
Moses said, "You want me to carry them to the land."
Moses said, "You swore to give this land to their fathers."
passages.original: הֶאָנֹכִ֣י הָרִ֗יתִי אֵ֚ת כָּל־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אִם־ אָנֹכִ֖י יְלִדְתִּ֑יהוּ כִּֽי־ תֹאמַ֨ר אֵלַ֜י שָׂאֵ֣הוּ בְחֵיקֶ֗ךָ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר יִשָּׂ֤א הָאֹמֵן֙ אֶת־ הַיֹּנֵ֔ק עַ֚ל הָֽאֲדָמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר נִשְׁבַּ֖עְתָּ לַאֲבֹתָֽיו׃

passages.text: Where can I get meat for all these people? For they keep crying out to me, ‘Give us meat to eat!’
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses led the people of Israel.
Moses said, "I do not have meat for all these people."
The people of Israel asked Moses for meat.
They cried out to Moses.
They said, 'Give us meat to eat.'
passages.original: מֵאַ֤יִן לִי֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר לָתֵ֖ת לְכָל־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּֽי־ יִבְכּ֤וּ עָלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תְּנָה־ לָּ֥נוּ בָשָׂ֖ר וְנֹאכֵֽלָה׃

passages.text: I cannot carry all these people by myself; it is too burdensome for me.
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to God.
Moses led the people of Israel.
Moses said, “I cannot carry all these people alone.
This burden is too heavy for me.”
passages.original: לֹֽא־ אוּכַ֤ל אָנֹכִי֙ לְבַדִּ֔י לָשֵׂ֖את אֶת־ כָּל־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה כִּ֥י כָבֵ֖ד מִמֶּֽנִּי׃

passages.text: If this is how You are going to treat me, please kill me right now—if I have found favor in Your eyes—and let me not see my own wretchedness.”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses spoke to God.
Moses felt overwhelmed by the people's complaints.
Moses said to God, "If You will treat me this way, kill me now."
Moses asked God to do this if he had found favor in God's eyes.
Moses did not want to see his own misery.
passages.original: וְאִם־ כָּ֣כָה׀ אַתְּ־ עֹ֣שֶׂה לִּ֗י הָרְגֵ֤נִי נָא֙ הָרֹ֔ג אִם־ מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ וְאַל־ אֶרְאֶ֖ה בְּרָעָתִֽי׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Bring Me seventy of the elders of Israel known to you as leaders and officers of the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting and have them stand there with you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to gather seventy men.
These men were elders of Israel.
These men were known to Moses as leaders and officers of the people.
The LORD told Moses to bring these seventy elders to Him.
The LORD told Moses to bring them to the Tent of Meeting.
The LORD told Moses to have them stand there with him.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶסְפָה־ לִּ֞י שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִישׁ֮ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּי־ הֵ֛ם זִקְנֵ֥י הָעָ֖ם וְשֹׁטְרָ֑יו וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אֹתָם֙ אֶל־ אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וְהִֽתְיַצְּב֥וּ שָׁ֖ם עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: And I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put that Spirit on them. They will help you bear the burden of the people, so that you do not have to bear it by yourself.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD said, “I will come down to you there.
I will speak with you at that place.
I will take some of the Spirit that is on you.
I will put that Spirit on the seventy elders.
These elders are leaders and officers of Israel.
They will help you carry the burden of the people.
You will not carry the burden alone.”
passages.original: וְיָרַדְתִּ֗י וְדִבַּרְתִּ֣י עִמְּךָ֮ שָׁם֒ וְאָצַלְתִּ֗י מִן־ הָר֛וּחַ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָלֶ֖יךָ וְשַׂמְתִּ֣י עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וְנָשְׂא֤וּ אִתְּךָ֙ בְּמַשָּׂ֣א הָעָ֔ם וְלֹא־ תִשָּׂ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לְבַדֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: And say to the people: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat, because you have cried out in the hearing of the LORD, saying: ‘Who will feed us meat? For we were better off in Egypt!’ Therefore the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God told Moses to speak to the people of Israel.
Moses must tell the people to prepare themselves for tomorrow.
God commands the people to set themselves apart.
Tomorrow, the people will eat meat.
The people cried out to God.
The people said, “Who will give us meat to eat?”
The people said, “It was better for us in Egypt.”
God heard the people’s complaint.
God will give the people meat.
The people will eat the meat God gives.
passages.original: וְאֶל־ הָעָ֨ם תֹּאמַ֜ר הִתְקַדְּשׁ֣וּ לְמָחָר֮ וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֣ם בָּשָׂר֒ כִּ֡י בְּכִיתֶם֩ בְּאָזְנֵ֨י יְהוָ֜ה לֵאמֹ֗ר מִ֤י יַאֲכִלֵ֙נוּ֙ בָּשָׂ֔ר כִּי־ ט֥וֹב לָ֖נוּ בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם וְנָתַ֨ן יְהוָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וַאֲכַלְתֶּֽם׃

passages.text: You will eat it not for one or two days, nor for five or ten or twenty days, but for a whole month—until it comes out of your nostrils and makes you nauseous—because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have cried out before Him, saying, ‘Why did we ever leave Egypt?’ ”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to the people of Israel.
God said they would eat meat.
They would not eat meat for only one day.
They would not eat meat for only two days.
They would not eat meat for only five days.
They would not eat meat for only ten days.
They would not eat meat for only twenty days.
They would eat meat for a whole month.
They would eat meat until it came out of their nostrils.
The meat would become disgusting to them.
This would happen because they rejected the LORD.
The LORD was among them.
They cried out before the LORD.
They said, "Why did we ever leave Egypt?"
passages.original: לֹ֣א י֥וֹם אֶחָ֛ד תֹּאכְל֖וּן וְלֹ֣א יוֹמָ֑יִם וְלֹ֣א׀ חֲמִשָּׁ֣ה יָמִ֗ים וְלֹא֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה יָמִ֔ים וְלֹ֖א עֶשְׂרִ֥ים יֽוֹם׃ עַ֣ד׀ חֹ֣דֶשׁ יָמִ֗ים עַ֤ד אֲשֶׁר־ יֵצֵא֙ מֵֽאַפְּכֶ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם לְזָרָ֑א יַ֗עַן כִּֽי־ מְאַסְתֶּ֤ם אֶת־ יְהוָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּקִרְבְּכֶ֔ם וַתִּבְכּ֤וּ לְפָנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֥מָּה זֶּ֖ה יָצָ֥אנוּ מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: But Moses replied, “Here I am among 600,000 men on foot, yet You say, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a month.’
passages.sermon:
Moses spoke to the LORD.
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
There were 600,000 men on foot among the people.
Moses was in the midst of these people.
Moses said, “You have said, ‘I will give them meat.’
You have said, ‘They will eat for a month.’”
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ מֹשֶׁה֒ שֵׁשׁ־ מֵא֥וֹת אֶ֙לֶף֙ רַגְלִ֔י הָעָ֕ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר אָנֹכִ֖י בְּקִרְבּ֑וֹ וְאַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֗רְתָּ בָּשָׂר֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם וְאָכְל֖וּ חֹ֥דֶשׁ יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: If all our flocks and herds were slaughtered for them, would they have enough? Or if all the fish in the sea were caught for them, would they have enough?”
passages.sermon:
Moses led the people of Israel in the wilderness.
He spoke to God about the people's needs.
Moses said, "If we slaughter all our sheep and cattle for the people, will that be enough for them?"
He also said, "If we gather all the fish from the sea for the people, will that be enough for them?"
passages.original: הֲצֹ֧אן וּבָקָ֛ר יִשָּׁחֵ֥ט לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֣א לָהֶ֑ם אִ֣ם אֶֽת־ כָּל־ דְּגֵ֥י הַיָּ֛ם יֵאָסֵ֥ף לָהֶ֖ם וּמָצָ֥א לָהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: The LORD answered Moses, “Is the LORD’s arm too short? Now you will see whether or not My word will come to pass.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD is powerful.
The LORD asked Moses a question.
The LORD said, “Is the LORD’s arm too short?”
The LORD can do anything.
The LORD said, “Now you will see if My word comes true.”
The LORD promised to show Moses what He can do.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הֲיַ֥ד יְהוָ֖ה תִּקְצָ֑ר עַתָּ֥ה תִרְאֶ֛ה הֲיִקְרְךָ֥ דְבָרִ֖י אִם־ לֹֽא׃

passages.text: So Moses went out and relayed to the people the words of the LORD, and he gathered seventy of the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of the Israelites.
Moses went out from his place.
He spoke to the people.
He told them the words of the LORD.
He gathered seventy elders from among the people.
He made the seventy elders stand around the tent.
passages.original: וַיֵּצֵ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה וַיְדַבֵּר֙ אֶל־ הָעָ֔ם אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וַיֶּאֱסֹ֞ף שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מִזִּקְנֵ֣י הָעָ֔ם וַֽיַּעֲמֵ֥ד אֹתָ֖ם סְבִיבֹ֥ת הָאֹֽהֶל׃

passages.text: Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and placed that Spirit on the seventy elders. As the Spirit rested on them, they prophesied—but they never did so again.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD came down in a cloud.
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD took some of the Spirit that was on Moses.
The LORD put that Spirit on seventy elders of the people.
The Spirit rested on the seventy elders.
The seventy elders began to prophesy.
They did not prophesy again after that.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֨רֶד יְהוָ֥ה׀ בֶּעָנָן֮ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָיו֒ וַיָּ֗אצֶל מִן־ הָר֙וּחַ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָלָ֔יו וַיִּתֵּ֕ן עַל־ שִׁבְעִ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ הַזְּקֵנִ֑ים וַיְהִ֗י כְּנ֤וֹחַ עֲלֵיהֶם֙ הָר֔וּחַ וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ וְלֹ֥א יָסָֽפוּ׃

passages.text: Two men, however, had remained in the camp—one named Eldad and the other Medad—and the Spirit rested on them. They were among those listed, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
passages.sermon:
Two men stayed in the camp.
The first man was named Eldad.
The second man was named Medad.
The Spirit rested on Eldad and Medad.
Eldad and Medad were among those who were chosen.
They did not go out to the tent.
Eldad and Medad prophesied in the camp.
passages.original: וַיִּשָּׁאֲר֣וּ שְׁנֵֽי־ אֲנָשִׁ֣ים׀ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֡ה שֵׁ֣ם הָאֶחָ֣ד׀ אֶלְדָּ֡ד וְשֵׁם֩ הַשֵּׁנִ֨י מֵידָ֜ד וַתָּ֧נַח עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם הָר֗וּחַ וְהֵ֙מָּה֙ בַּכְּתֻבִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָצְא֖וּ הָאֹ֑הֱלָה וַיִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וּ בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: A young man ran and reported to Moses, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
passages.sermon:
A young man saw something important.
He ran quickly to Moses.
He spoke to Moses.
He said, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
passages.original: וַיָּ֣רָץ הַנַּ֔עַר וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לְמֹשֶׁ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֶלְדָּ֣ד וּמֵידָ֔ד מִֽתְנַבְּאִ֖ים בַּֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: Joshua son of Nun, the attendant to Moses since youth, spoke up and said, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”
passages.sermon:
Joshua was the son of Nun.
Joshua had served Moses since he was young.
Joshua was Moses’ attendant.
Joshua spoke up.
Joshua said, “Moses, my lord, stop them!”
passages.original: וַיַּ֜עַן יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בִּן־ נ֗וּן מְשָׁרֵ֥ת מֹשֶׁ֛ה מִבְּחֻרָ֖יו וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֲדֹנִ֥י מֹשֶׁ֖ה כְּלָאֵֽם׃

passages.text: But Moses replied, “Are you jealous on my account? I wish that all the LORD’s people were prophets and that the LORD would place His Spirit on them!”
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Joshua was Moses’ assistant.
Joshua spoke to Moses.
Joshua wanted Moses to stop Eldad and Medad from prophesying.
Moses replied to Joshua.
Moses asked, “Are you jealous for me?”
Moses wished for something greater.
Moses said, “I wish all the LORD’s people were prophets.”
Moses wanted the LORD to give His Spirit to all the people.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ מֹשֶׁ֔ה הַֽמְקַנֵּ֥א אַתָּ֖ה לִ֑י וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן כָּל־ עַ֤ם יְהוָה֙ נְבִיאִ֔ים כִּי־ יִתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ רוּח֖וֹ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Then Moses returned to the camp, along with the elders of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Moses was the leader of Israel.
Moses returned to the camp.
The elders of Israel went with Moses.
passages.original: וַיֵּאָסֵ֥ף מֹשֶׁ֖ה אֶל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה ה֖וּא וְזִקְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Now a wind sent by the LORD came up, drove in quail from the sea, and brought them near the camp, about two cubits above the surface of the ground, for a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.
passages.sermon:
The LORD sent a wind.
The wind came from the LORD.
The wind brought quail from the sea.
The wind drove the quail toward the camp.
The quail landed near the camp.
The quail surrounded the camp.
The quail covered the ground for a day’s journey in every direction around the camp.
The quail lay about two cubits above the surface of the ground.
passages.original: וְר֜וּחַ נָסַ֣ע׀ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּ֣גָז שַׂלְוִים֮ מִן־ הַיָּם֒ וַיִּטֹּ֨שׁ עַל־ הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֜ה כְּדֶ֧רֶךְ י֣וֹם כֹּ֗ה וּכְדֶ֤רֶךְ יוֹם֙ כֹּ֔ה סְבִיב֖וֹת הַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה וּכְאַמָּתַ֖יִם עַל־ פְּנֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: All that day and night, and all the next day, the people stayed up gathering the quail. No one gathered less than ten homers, and they spread them out all around the camp.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel gathered quail.
They worked all that day.
They worked all that night.
They worked all the next day.
Each person gathered quail.
No one gathered less than ten homers.
They spread the quail out around the camp.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣קָם הָעָ֡ם כָּל־ הַיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא וְכָל־ הַלַּ֜יְלָה וְכֹ֣ל׀ י֣וֹם הַֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַיַּֽאַסְפוּ֙ אֶת־ הַשְּׂלָ֔ו הַמַּמְעִ֕יט אָסַ֖ף עֲשָׂרָ֣ה חֳמָרִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁטְח֤וּ לָהֶם֙ שָׁט֔וֹחַ סְבִיב֖וֹת הַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

passages.text: But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the anger of the LORD burned against the people, and the LORD struck them with a severe plague.
passages.sermon:
The people ate meat.
The meat was still between their teeth.
They had not yet chewed it.
The LORD became very angry with the people.
The LORD struck the people with a severe plague.
passages.original: הַבָּשָׂ֗ר עוֹדֶ֙נּוּ֙ בֵּ֣ין שִׁנֵּיהֶ֔ם טֶ֖רֶם יִכָּרֵ֑ת וְאַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ חָרָ֣ה בָעָ֔ם וַיַּ֤ךְ יְהוָה֙ בָּעָ֔ם מַכָּ֖ה רַבָּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: So they called that place Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel traveled in the wilderness.
Some people among them craved other food.
God sent quail for them to eat.
While they ate the meat, God struck them with a severe plague.
Many people died there because of their craving.
The people named that place Kibroth-hattaavah.
Kibroth-hattaavah means "graves of craving."
They called it this because they buried the people who craved other food there.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת־ שֵֽׁם־ הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא קִבְר֣וֹת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֑ה כִּי־ שָׁם֙ קָֽבְר֔וּ אֶת־ הָעָ֖ם הַמִּתְאַוִּֽים׃

passages.text: From Kibroth-hattaavah the people moved on to Hazeroth, where they remained for some time.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites were traveling in the wilderness.
They left Kibroth-hattaavah.
They moved to Hazeroth.
They stayed in Hazeroth for a while.
passages.original: מִקִּבְר֧וֹת הַֽתַּאֲוָ֛ה נָסְע֥וּ הָעָ֖ם חֲצֵר֑וֹת וַיִּהְי֖וּ בַּחֲצֵרֽוֹת׃פ
